newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends lower, rumoured Skikda trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends lower, rumoured Skikda trade.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices trimmed their losses to end slightly lower on Monday after crude oil rebounded smartly in late action.
One source said there were rumours that a Spanish end-user sold a Skikda cargo for loading Feb 5-9 to be loaded together with another cargo to be sent to the U.S.
The two stems totalling 60,000 tonnes would be the first of its kind since early December and potentially bullish, he said.
The deal could not be confirmed.
But, as underlined during last week's activity, the high freight rates, particularly in the Med, and quiet end-user demand were suffocating physical trading.
"The basic situation has been that it is difficult to find vessels," a trader said. "It is not a problem of money. It is a problem of availability."
Skikda and Alexandria material was available, but the shortage of vessels was pushing traders out of a market already limited by quiet end-user demand, he said.
Feb swaps ended $2 lower at $218/$219 a tonne, trimming about $1 off its lows for the day when IPE Brent futures rebounded off support at $22 a barrel.
NWE cargoes notionally ended unchanged to slightly lower at $218/$222 cif, with Med cargoes at $215/$217.
"There is not much end-user demand in the Med so the market is balanced," the trader said. He said the arbitrage from the Med to the U.S. was shut.
